description: Replace the ReLU-squared MLP with a SwiGLU gate (SiLU(gate) * up), with hidden width set to about 8/3 * n_embd rounded up to a multiple of 128 so the parameter count stays close to the baseline.
Reduce the warmdown ratio to 0.2 to maintain a higher learning rate for a longer duration during the final training phase.

Aborted the "Add Residual Attention" idea because train.py already routes attention through a residual connection (x = x + attn(norm(x)) in Block, plus the ResFormer value residual), so the spec adds nothing new without a costly change.
Apply weight decay only to residual lambdas layer to reduce overfitting with minimal regularization.
Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine annealing schedule to improve learning rate stability during the final phase of training.

Integrate a simple gradient norm-based adaptive learning rate schedule that scales the current step's learning rate by the minimum of 1.0 and the inverse square root of the gradient norm, reducing loss overfitting while maintaining update speed.

Removes the undefined gnorm_sum call (and the unused adaptive-LR computation built on it) from the Muon branch of the training loop, and sets the Muon group's LR to the scheduled base_lr so the warmdown still applies.

issues: Integrity is fine. The diff changes only the WEIGHT_DECAY hyperparameter (0.2 to 0.01) and its comment. It doesn't touch the evaluation path, the data, the seed lines or the prepare.py import line, and the harness raised no integrity flags.
No bugs found that would make the result meaningless. This is a single hyperparameter change.

The new comment says the lower weight decay will 'allow faster convergence', but the numbers don't support it. The candidate's val_bpb is 1.1178, which is worse than the incumbent mean of 1.1146 (+0.0032, and lower is better).

z can't be recomputed independently because the incumbent's standard deviation or standard error isn't given. The reported z = -0.594 has the right sign for a worse candidate. If z is the gap divided by the incumbent's spread, that spread would be about 0.0054.
The candidate has only one run (n=1), so the evidence is weak either way. Still, nothing suggests an improvement, and the provisional reject decision holds.

description: Reduce weight decay to 0.01 to allow faster convergence with less regularization while maintaining model quality.
Add a dropout layer immediately after the attention branch in the Block module to regularize early layers.
Skip the loss-scaling idea: a constant 2.0 multiplier on the loss is effectively a no-op in this training setup, so it would spend a slot without testing anything.

Set HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 so the 512-dim model gets 8 heads of width 64 instead of 4 of width 128; this does not reduce parameter count, since projection shapes stay the same, so only the attention head split changes.
Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine annealing schedule to provide a smoother learning rate decay.
Fix the warmdown crash by using math.cos instead of torch.cos, since phase_progress is a Python float and not a tensor.
Replace the AdamW step fused function with an Adamp-smoothed variant that adds the squared gradient to the second moment buffer to reduce variance.
Lower the Muon matrix LR and the embedding Adam LR, which were too high for this model and caused the loss blow-up at step 85, and add a short warmup so the early updates are gentler.

Abort the Residual Connection idea because train.py already has residual connections around both the attention and MLP sublayers in Block.forward, plus learned per-layer residual scaling (resid_lambdas) and x0 skip connections.
Replicate the SwiGLU MLP by replacing ReLU-squared with SiLU * linear to lower val_bpb.

Introduce weights exponential bias-squared (EBSQ) on linear layers by scaling them with exp(-|W|/tau) in the forward pass, and adjusting the learning rate by the median of these factors to avoid divergent updates.

The MLP multiplied activations of shape (B, T, 4*n_embd) by a weight-shaped (out, in) tensor, which cannot broadcast; I moved the weight-dependent damping into the weights themselves and used F.linear, so the shapes are correct and the idea is preserved.
Increase the WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.1 to allow for better initialization of Adam states during the early training phase.
Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2^20 and set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 64 with gradient accumulation=8 to fit on 40GB while attempting to lower val_bpb.

Pin the Muon learning rate for the attention weights (c_q, c_k, c_v, c_proj, ve_gate) to a fixed constant of 0.01 that ignores the LR warmdown, while MLP and other matrices keep the scheduled matrix_lr.

Add stochastic depth by dropping each Block's whole residual update (attention and MLP together) with probability 0.5 during training, using an inverted 1/keep scale and a tensor-valued mask so torch.compile does not graph-break.
